expectations.text: Response distinguishes between building mode (frames scattered, some building, labels missing) and judging mode (all iframes live, zones labeled and numbered, focusCanvasShapes called), and says to switch to judging mode before any public review.
expectations.evidence: Response describes organizing canvas sections (header, user flow, key screens) in Figma/design-tool terms — no mention of building vs judging mode, no mention of focusCanvasShapes, no mention of iframe 'live' state requirement.

expectations.text: Response describes the hero row with the three primary deliverables: the interactive app, the pitch deck (slides), and the showcase video — placed at y = 100 with a section label above at y = 20.
expectations.evidence: No hero row described. No y-coordinate positioning. Response suggests a 'Header/Title block' at the top with project name — a completely different concept. The three-artifact hero row layout (web + slides + video) is not mentioned.

expectations.text: Response specifies the zone label convention: text shape, color: 'grey', h: 60, placed 40 units above the zone's frame baseline, numbered with pattern '01 — ZONE NAME'.
expectations.evidence: No zone label convention described. Response says to 'give every frame a clear, descriptive name' (e.g. 'Home', 'Dashboard') — a different labeling concept with no color, height, position, or numbering specification.

expectations.text: Response specifies standard gutters: 80 px between sibling frames (within the same zone) and 160 px between zones.
expectations.evidence: No gutter values mentioned. Response says to 'align and evenly space frames' without specific pixel values.

needs_review: Without-skill describes Figma/Framer canvas conventions — no Replit Canvas API knowledge at all. A developer following this advice would have no idea how to set up a Replit Canvas board for judges.
